disagreements.topic: Has a Nutrition separation actually been announced, and does it belong in value?
disagreements.positions: All five treat a Nutrition spin by end-2027 as announced; agents 1/4 deduct separation cash (-$320M/-$400M), agent_3 puts $350M in FY27 other_uses, agents 2/5 nothing; ladder branches 10-12%.
disagreements.resolution: Confirmed at the primary source: Abbott 8-K (CIK 1800, accession 0001104659-26-117587, filed 2026-10-21) Ex. 99.1 announces the intention to separate Nutrition (~$8.5B sales) via a tax-free distribution, expected by end-2027, one-time charges to be quantified; CFO on the call: costs are specified items excluded from adjusted EPS. Value-neutral to holders, so it is not in the research target (12m) except -$300M after-tax separation cash; kept as a 10% ladder branch (judgment: Abbott expects completion by end-2027 and the horizon is 2027-10-20, ~2.4 months before the end of that window; the agents gave 10-12%). Quote ~$9 lower if distributed before the horizon: the mean of agent_1's ($1.65B EBITDA x 14x - $4.5B debt) / 1,729M = $10.7 and agent_5's (($1,540M - $150M) x 12x - $4B) / 1,725M = $7.35 derivations, low confidence. [citation gate 2026-10-21: the unsourced 14-21 month base rate is removed]

disagreements.positions: All agents use ~$670M NEC and $384.2M DOJ/states; after-tax treatment -$520M to -$566M and -$345M to -$350M; agents 3/5 carry them in FY26 other_uses instead of adjustments.
disagreements.resolution: Both confirmed at primary sources: 8-K 2026-08-20 says ~$670M aggregate for Gill (~$600M judgment plus interest) and ~2,000 infants, leaving ~1,700 suits / ~12,700 infants; CA AG 2026-09-21: $348,700,868 federal + $35,491,288 states = $384,192,156. CURRENT (2026-11-18, balance 2026-09-30): the DOJ / states settlement was paid in September and is in the 2026-09-30 net debt, so it has no adjustment; of the NEC charge, at most the $435M total legal accrual at 2026-09-30 is unpaid (10-Q R21): -$435M x (1 - ~22.5%) = -$337M after tax; the remaining NEC claims are -$750M; total adjustments -$2,017M (inputs_detail 'adjustments'). SUPERSEDED: -$520M and -$350M as adjustments on the 2026-06-30 balance.

disagreements.positions: agent_2 -$700M, agent_4 -$750M, agent_1 -$875M, agent_3 -$900M, agent_5 -$950M (after tax).
disagreements.resolution: The August deal implies ~$35k per non-Gill infant (($670M - ~$600M)/~2,000); the 8-K says the remaining 12,700 include duplicate and non-NEC claims. -$750M after tax (~$76k per infant, ~2x the deal rate, for verdict risk and defense) with low confidence; range -$450M to -$1.5B moves value only -$0.25 to +$0.20/share.

It would not surprise me at all that we would do better.' (same call), naming payer formulary coverage that 'flipped in our favor' from 2027-01-01 and the Libre Duo US launch (December 2026). The guide range is not used for FY2027. FY2028-29 underlying growth = the same Fortune pair, US 10.1% and international 10.1% (implied), = 10.1%, with no further Abbott price concession (the CEO's 'couple of quarters' ends inside FY2027), booked pending Kilian (card 'cgm' FY2028-29). Evidence around it, sized as alternatives: Abbott's own 9M 2026 US +9.3% and international +6.6% comparable (src 1), Dexcom's Q3 2026 US +14% and international +5% (src 81), Fortune's Europe 8.4% (src 118), Mordor's US 18.23% and global 15.09% (src 93, 132) and the round-6 placeholder (US +8% / international +3%, no source). Reconciliation with actuals: Fortune's own 2026 market grows 12.0% (USD 13.86B to 15.52B) against the two leaders' 2026 reported growth of about 10-13% (Abbott Diabetes Care +10.0% reported in 9M 2026, src 1; Dexcom's FY2026 guide of about 12-13%, src 81), so the actuals have not overtaken Fortune's path; the page was updated after both Q3 prints. FY2028 less a Medicare price step of 1.69% of CGM sales: the remote-item-delivery bid round resets CGM payment amounts once from 2028-01-01 at the 75th percentile of winning bids, then CPI updates (CMS final rule, src 53). Size = US share of Libre (40%) x Medicare share of US CGM dollars (~20.7% = Part B CGM payments $1.3B in 2023, HHS OIG via src 83, over Mordor's US CGM market of $6.28B in 2025, src 93; Mordor gives no 2023 or 2024 value and OIG no 2025 value, so the years do not match, and with Medicare CGM payments up from $109M in 2018 to $1.3B in 2023 (src 83) the 2025 share may be higher; low confidence) x the cut that reaches Abbott's own price, 20.4% (gate fix round 8, pending Kilian, card 'cgm' Medicare), sized from two sources because none gives it directly: (a) the most a bid round can take out of the supplier channel before suppliers sell below cost is the overpayment OIG measured, 69% above acquisition cost (src 83), i.e. 0.69 / 1.69 = 40.8% of the Medicare payment; (b) of any cut, Raymond James 'expects that medical equipment distributors will shoulder a good portion of any price erosion' and calls Abbott, 'as the lower cost player, ... better positioned than DexCom in a competitive bidding world' (Barron's 2025-07-01, src 142), JPMorgan expects less impact on Abbott than on Dexcom (src 83), and Dexcom's IR says it feels good about 'the balance of economics between us and the durable-medical-equipment distributors' (src 142). Read as the distributors taking at least half, Abbott bears at most half: 40.8% x 1/2 = 20.4%. Both factors sit at the costly end of what the sources allow (the whole overpayment removed, the largest maker share 'a good portion' leaves), so the step is the moderately conservative end; step = 0.40 x 20.7% x 20.4% = 1.69% of CGM sales (was 0.83% on an unsourced 10% pass-through). Core Laboratory FY2027-29 +3% a year at constant currency, booked pending Kilian (card 'dx_base'): the only forward source for the category is Roche's Diagnostics Day outlook, which revised its Core Lab growth to a 3% CAGR for China market headwinds (Roche Diagnostics Day 2026-05-18, src 97); Abbott also sells Core Lab into China, where pricing reforms cut Roche's Asia-Pacific sales 4% in 9M 2026 (src 71). The CEO says test volumes are 'healthy and at durable levels' (Q3 2026 call, https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/abt/transcripts/709642-q3-2026/) but gives no rate. Abbott's own Core Laboratory 9M 2026 comparable growth of +4.0% (src 1) and Roche's Core Lab +5% CER in 9M 2026 (src 71) are past periods, so they are options on the card, not the booked level (moderately conservative: the forward source, below both). Rapid and Molecular +5% a year FY2027-29 at constant currency (gate fix round 7), booked pending Kilian (card 'dx_base'): no forward source gives Abbott's own Rapid or Molecular growth, and the round-6 placeholder held two of Roche's past nine-month rates for four forecast periods, which the rules do not allow. The forward evidence: rapid diagnostic kits 8.27% a year 2026-31 (Mordor Intelligence, July 2026, src 95), molecular diagnostics 8.5% 2026-31 (MarketsandMarkets, November 2026, src 96), point-of-care diagnostics 8.8% 2026-31 (MarketsandMarkets, src 85), and Roche expects its Diagnostics division to grow mid to high single digits (Diagnostics Day 2026-05-18, no timeframe stated, src 97), the nearest forward statement by a direct competitor. Abbott's Rapid and Molecular sales fell 5.4% comparable in 9M 2026 (src 1) and Roche's Near Patient Care fell 5% CER (src 71) as respiratory testing shrank, so the line has lagged the market forecasts; the booked rate is the low end of Roche's forward outlook ('mid' single digits, 5%), below every market forecast (8.27-8.8%) and Roche's 'high' end (moderately conservative). The sub-line market build (+8.4%), Roche's outlook middle (+6%), Roche's 9M division rate (+4%) and the round-6 placeholder on Roche's past areas (-1.51%) are on the card. Peak sales = coronary IVL market at peak x Abbott share. Market: Shockwave (J&J) passed $1B in 2025, IVL +23% in Q4 2025 (src 38); the program is US only, and US coronary was 56.7% of Shockwave sales in Q4 2023 ($115.2M of the $152.9M coronary, out of $203M total, src 39; all coronary was 75%), so 2025 US coronary IVL is about 0.567 x $1.0B = $0.57B (derived; gate fix round 7, was the global coronary $0.75B). At the intravascular lithotripsy market's 11.5% a year 2026-33 (Grand View Research, published 2026-10-21, src 149, the newest IVL forecast found; it replaces Global Market Insights' July 2026 15.8% 2026-35, src 131, sized as an alternative; coronary and peripheral together, as no coronary-only forecast with a consistent base was found: Persistence's coronary IVL page, February 2026, gives both 5.5% and 4.3% on a USD 371M 2026 market below Shockwave's own sales) the US coronary market is about 0.567 x 1.115^7 = $1.22B by 2032 (global coronary 0.75 x 1.115^7 = $1.61B, about 32% of the >$5B coronary TAM in Shockwave's FY2023 10-K, src 40). Price cross-check: $4,700 per catheter (2021, src 41) gives ~259k US catheters a year at $1.22B. Abbott share at peak 15% (JUDGMENT): four entrants by then (J&J incumbent; Boston Scientific via Bolt/Seismiq, src 43; its FRACTURE IDE pivotal for SEISMIQ 4CE met both primary endpoints 2026-05-19, src 44; Elixir LithiX, full European market release 2025-10-03 after an April 2025 CE mark, src 46; Abbott), Abbott helped by its XIENCE stent and OCT imaging position in the same cath labs (src 42) and by the Federal Circuit 2025-07-14 ruling (Shockwave Medical v. Stewart) that claims 1-17 of Shockwave's U.S. Patent 8,956,371 are unpatentable (claims 1-4, 6-17 affirmed, claim 5 reversed; src 45) (Abbott-owned CSI was the challenger). 0.15 x $1.215B = $182.2M (gate fix round 9; $237.7M at GMI's 15.8%). US only: no CE mark or OUS plan found (src 42). Launch 2027-06-30 = end of the CEO's first-half window (approval timing is the CEO's expectation, not an FDA date). Ramp 5 years (Shockwave took ~5 years from US coronary approval in Feb 2021 to ~$0.75B; judgment for a follower). Margin 34% = the set's Medical Devices segment operating margin (m_dev, FY2027 ~34%); IVL gross margins run 87-88% (Shockwave, src 39), so mature-year margin is likely higher and launch years lower (JUDGMENT). Tax 15.5% = the set's adjusted rate. P(approval) 0.85 (JUDGMENT): both pivotal endpoints met and the PMA is filed; residual risk is an FDA deficiency letter, panel or a narrower label. Discount 11.14% = ABT cost of equity on the house ERP line: rf 4.929% (10y UST 2026-10-30, engine) + 7.69% x (0.768 + 0.232 x beta 0.17). Erosion 2039: no IP-life evidence; next-generation IVL and price competition after ~12 years (JUDGMENT). Development costs: TECTONIC is done; remaining launch cost sits inside the margin (0). No overlap with driver:cv_other: it is a category build (Vascular +5.17% a year at the coronary stent and peripheral vascular market forecasts, mix 6.09% / 6.17% / 6.24% FY2027-29) with coronary IVL excluded and valued here only. Peripheral IVL (trial to start at year end, src 37) is not booked: no trial, no probability evidence yet.

drivers.derivation: FY2026 = 9M 6,453 (src 1) + Q4 2,185.4: Q4 FY2025 2,133 (10-K less 9M) grown +3.5% at constant currency, the middle of the CEO's 'low to mid-single' range for Q4 'and probably for the next few quarters' (Q3 2026 call, https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/abt/transcripts/709642-q3-2026/), less 1.04pt FX (60% international; Q4 FY2026 FX: the CFO's ~-1% on Q4 company sales at current rates (Q3 2026 call, https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/abt/transcripts/709642-q3-2026/) scaled by each line's international share against the company's 57.7% (Q3 2026 international 7,509 / 13,013, src 1).); a declared guide use (guidance_check 'Diabetes Care (CGM) sales growth'). FY2027 +8.00% at constant currency, built from the forward market forecasts by region on Q3 2026 weights (US 872 = 40%, international 1,313 = 60%, src 1) and booked pending Kilian (card 'cgm' FY2027). Both regions sit on one publisher's global / US pair (gate fix round 7): Fortune Business Insights (page updated 2026-11-02, src 118) gives the global CGM market USD 15.52B in 2026 growing 10.1% a year 2026-34, of which the US is USD 6.29B (40.5%), and gives no separate US rate; so the US is booked at the global 10.1% and the international rate implied by that same pair is (10.1% - 0.405 x 10.1%) / (1 - 0.405) = 10.1%, which together give back the 10.1% global rate (Fortune's Europe rate, 8.4% a year, the only regional rate on the page, is a cross-check). Fortune is the newest edition found and the lowest current global forecast: Mordor's global CGM market grows 15.09% a year 2027-32 (page updated 2026-10-22, src 132), and IMARC 4.38% 2026-34 and Global Market Insights 16.3% 2026-35 (src 115, 114) are April 2026 editions past their window. Mordor's US CGM market, 18.23% a year 2026-31 (src 93), is not booked: its own 2026 value (USD 6.28B in 2025 to 7.43B in 2026, +18.3%) runs well above what the two US leaders report for 2026 (Abbott US Diabetes Care +9.3% in 9M 2026, src 1; Dexcom US +14% in Q3 2026, src 81), so the actuals released since its August 2026 edition have overtaken its near-term path; booked beside Fortune's global rate it would also imply an ex-US market of (10.1% - 0.405 x 18.23%) / (1 - 0.405) = +4.56%, a pair no single publisher gives (Mordor's own pair, global 15.09% and US 18.23%, implies 12.9% ex-US; both are alternatives on the card). Less Abbott's own international price concession: the CEO is adjusting international prices 'a little bit' to hold 50-70% share, which will 'mute a little bit of the volume growth', with 'a little bit of an impact for a couple of quarters, and then you kind of reignite' (Q3 2026 call, https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/abt/transcripts/709642-q3-2026/). No source gives its size, so it is sized as well as the sources allow: CGM grew 7.7% comparable in Q3 2026 (Q3 release text, src 1: 'sales of continuous glucose monitors grew 7.3 percent on a reported basis and 7.7 percent on a comparable basis'; the CEO rounds it to 8%; the Diabetes Care table line, which also holds blood-glucose meters, grew 6.7% comparable in Q3 and 7.7% in 9M 2026), and the middle of the CEO's Q4 range is +3.5%: a 4.2pt slowdown of total CGM, or 4.2 / 0.60 = 7.0pt of international sales, an upper bound for the price effect because the CEO also names slower type-2 penetration; 'a couple of quarters' from Q4 2026 puts up to two of them in FY2027, so the FY2027 concession = 7.0pt x 2/4 = 3.5pt of international sales (the moderately conservative end: largest size, both quarters in FY2027). International = 10.1% - 3.5% = 6.6%; FY2027 = 0.40 x 10.1% + 0.60 x 6.6% = +8.00%. Cross-checks (not inputs): in the two concession quarters international grows 10.1% - 7.0% = 3.1% and CGM 0.40 x 10.1% + 0.60 x 3.1% = 5.9%, inside the CEO's 'low to mid-single' range (read 1-6%) for Q4 'and probably for the next few quarters'; for the year he says 'Would I be surprised that we would do much better than that next year? It would not surprise me at all that we would do better.' (same call), naming payer formulary coverage that 'flipped in our favor' from 2027-01-01 and the Libre Duo US launch (December 2026). The guide range is not used for FY2027. FY2028-29 underlying growth = the same Fortune pair, US 10.1% and international 10.1% (implied), = 10.1%, with no further Abbott price concession (the CEO's 'couple of quarters' ends inside FY2027), booked pending Kilian (card 'cgm' FY2028-29). Evidence around it, sized as alternatives: Abbott's own 9M 2026 US +9.3% and international +6.6% comparable (src 1), Dexcom's Q3 2026 US +14% and international +5% (src 81), Fortune's Europe 8.4% (src 118), Mordor's US 18.23% and global 15.09% (src 93, 132) and the round-6 placeholder (US +8% / international +3%, no source). Reconciliation with actuals: Fortune's own 2026 market grows 12.0% (USD 13.86B to 15.52B) against the two leaders' 2026 reported growth of about 10-13% (Abbott Diabetes Care +10.0% reported in 9M 2026, src 1; Dexcom's FY2026 guide of about 12-13%, src 81), so the actuals have not overtaken Fortune's path; the page was updated after both Q3 prints. FY2028 less a Medicare price step of 1.69% of CGM sales: the remote-item-delivery bid round resets CGM payment amounts once from 2028-01-01 at the 75th percentile of winning bids, then CPI updates (CMS final rule, src 53). Size = US share of Libre (40%) x Medicare share of US CGM dollars (~20.7% = Part B CGM payments $1.3B in 2023, HHS OIG via src 83, over Mordor's US CGM market of $6.28B in 2025, src 93; Mordor gives no 2023 or 2024 value and OIG no 2025 value, so the years do not match, and with Medicare CGM payments up from $109M in 2018 to $1.3B in 2023 (src 83) the 2025 share may be higher; low confidence) x the cut that reaches Abbott's own price, 20.4% (gate fix round 8, pending Kilian, card 'cgm' Medicare), sized from two sources because none gives it directly: (a) the most a bid round can take out of the supplier channel before suppliers sell below cost is the overpayment OIG measured, 69% above acquisition cost (src 83), i.e. 0.69 / 1.69 = 40.8% of the Medicare payment; (b) of any cut, Raymond James 'expects that medical equipment distributors will shoulder a good portion of any price erosion' and calls Abbott, 'as the lower cost player, ... better positioned than DexCom in a competitive bidding world' (Barron's 2025-07-01, src 142), JPMorgan expects less impact on Abbott than on Dexcom (src 83), and Dexcom's IR says it feels good about 'the balance of economics between us and the durable-medical-equipment distributors' (src 142). Read as the distributors taking at least half, Abbott bears at most half: 40.8% x 1/2 = 20.4%. Both factors sit at the costly end of what the sources allow (the whole overpayment removed, the largest maker share 'a good portion' leaves), so the step is the moderately conservative end; step = 0.40 x 20.7% x 20.4% = 1.69% of CGM sales (was 0.83% on an unsourced 10% pass-through). Applied as a one-time level change from Q1 FY2028 (the reset date): every quarter from Q1 FY2028 is 1.53% below the pre-step path (1.69% / (1 + FY2028 pre-step growth)), so the FY2028 total is unchanged and FY2029 quarters grow at the step-free rate (gate fix round 8; the earlier build spread the step over FY2028's within-year path, which carried part of it into FY2029 y/y). A 10% pass-through, no step and the whole overpayment passed to Abbott (40.8%) are sized alternatives. The step is a one-time level reset, so FY2029 = the underlying 10.1%. drivers.derivation: Built by category from the 10-Q revenue note (Core Laboratory vs Rapid and Molecular). Core Laboratory FY2027-29 +3% a year at constant currency, booked pending Kilian (card 'dx_base'): the only forward source for the category is Roche's Diagnostics Day outlook, which revised its Core Lab growth to a 3% CAGR for China market headwinds (Roche Diagnostics Day 2026-05-18, src 97); Abbott also sells Core Lab into China, where pricing reforms cut Roche's Asia-Pacific sales 4% in 9M 2026 (src 71). The CEO says test volumes are 'healthy and at durable levels' (Q3 2026 call, https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/abt/transcripts/709642-q3-2026/) but gives no rate. Abbott's own Core Laboratory 9M 2026 comparable growth of +4.0% (src 1) and Roche's Core Lab +5% CER in 9M 2026 (src 71) are past periods, so they are options on the card, not the booked level (moderately conservative: the forward source, below both). Rapid and Molecular +5% a year FY2027-29 at constant currency (gate fix round 7), booked pending Kilian (card 'dx_base'): no forward source gives Abbott's own Rapid or Molecular growth, and the round-6 placeholder held two of Roche's past nine-month rates for four forecast periods, which the rules do not allow. The forward evidence: rapid diagnostic kits 8.27% a year 2026-31 (Mordor Intelligence, July 2026, src 95), molecular diagnostics 8.5% 2026-31 (MarketsandMarkets, November 2026, src 96), point-of-care diagnostics 8.8% 2026-31 (MarketsandMarkets, src 85), and Roche expects its Diagnostics division to grow mid to high single digits (Diagnostics Day 2026-05-18, no timeframe stated, src 97), the nearest forward statement by a direct competitor. Dated contracts: Florida's WIC contract for standard milk and soy formula moved to Abbott from 2026-02-01 (Florida DOH notice, src 78); Michigan's moves from Abbott to Mead Johnson from 2026-11-01 (Michigan DHHS memo, src 79); Michigan births are 44.4% of Florida's (99,525 vs 224,389 in 2024, KFF/CDC, src 77). The booked build treats the 5.6pt as contract-driven gains that annualize in February 2027 and sizes the Michigan loss at 0.444 x 5.6pt (two of three months in Q4 2026, ten months in FY2027): Q4 2026 US pediatric +9.34%, FY2027 +3.80%, FY2028-29 the market 5.4%. (2) International pediatric +4.5% ex-FX in Q4 FY2026 and +4.7% a year FY2027-29 (gate fix round 9): the global infant nutrition market grows 4.7% a year 2025-30 in value, with 4.5% in 2026 (Technavio, published 2026-09-03, src 147, the newest edition of the series found; it replaces Mordor's July 2026 7.69% 2026-31, src 121, a sized alternative; Market Glass's October 2026 clinical nutrition products report gives its infant nutrition product type 9.1% 2025-32, src 148, a clinical-nutrition segment rather than the whole infant market, sized as an upper bound), and the CEO says Nutrition's volume growth 'this quarter and what we're projecting to have in the next few quarters, it is significantly higher than what its peer set is' (Q3 2026 call); Abbott's Q3 2026 international pediatric grew +6.0% comparable (src 1), so the booked market rate is below Abbott's latest quarter (moderately conservative). (4) International adult: the clinical nutrition market grows 5.34% a year 2026-31 (Mordor Intelligence, page updated 2026-09-11, src 127; it supersedes Mordor's January 2026 edition (7.94%) and names Abbott among the leaders; Market Glass's newer global clinical nutrition products forecast, published 2026-10-01, src 148, gives 7.3% 2025-32 for the whole market including infant nutrition at 9.1%, and 5.3% for standard enteral formula, the segment closest to Abbott's adult line, which matches the 5.34%; adults 50.24% of 2025 demand, geriatric 9.16% a year), but Abbott's own line is below it: international adult fell 2.0% comparable in 9M 2026 and grew only +1.0% in Q3 (src 1), and the peers' latest quarter shows no jump: Nestle says 'adult nutrition slowed' in Q3 2026 while medical nutrition was strong (2026-10-22, src 141), and Danone's specialized nutrition grew 'strong mid-single digit' in China/North Asia (src 80). No source shows Abbott's line returning to the market rate from the next quarter (the round-7 booking) or within a year (the round-8 four-quarter phase-in): a search on 2026-11-18 (Abbott's Q3 2026 release and call, src 1 and src 52; NutraIngredients 2026-10-22 on Abbott's Q3 nutrition, international nutrition +3.1%; Nestle Q3 2026, src 141; Danone Q3 2026, src 80) found no statement on when international adult returns to its market, and the CEO's 'next few quarters' remark is about all of Nutrition's volume. (1) Cost of products sold 33.33% of sales, the Q3 FY2026 product cost ratio: Q3 rose 0.5pt above H1 2026 (32.82%) as CGM price concessions in international markets began earlier than the CEO expected; he says further concessions over the next few quarters will be offset 'through our COGS programs' (Q3 2026 call https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/abt/transcripts/709642-q3-2026/), so no net change and, moderately conservative, no return to the FY2025 32.6%. judgment_calls_for_kilian.question: How large is the FY2028 Medicare competitive-bidding price step on Libre CGM sales?
judgment_calls_for_kilian.context: CMS's remote-item-delivery competitive bidding round for CGMs sets new Medicare payment amounts once from 2028-01-01, at the 75th percentile of winning bids, then CPI updates (CMS final rule, DLA Piper summary). The size of the hit to Abbott = US share of Libre sales (40% on Q3 2026: US 872 of 2,185) x Medicare's share of US CGM dollars x the cut that passes through to Abbott's own price. Medicare share ~20.7% = Part B CGM payments $1.3B in 2023 (HHS OIG) over Mordor's US CGM market of $6.28B in 2025; Mordor gives no 2023 value and OIG no 2025 value, so the years do not match (low confidence). No source gives the pass-through as a number. Gate fix round 8 sizes it from what the sources do say: OIG found Medicare paid 69% more than suppliers' acquisition cost, so the most a bid round can take out of the supplier channel is 0.69 / 1.69 = 40.8% of the payment; Raymond James expects 'medical equipment distributors will shoulder a good portion of any price erosion' and calls Abbott, 'as the lower cost player', better positioned than Dexcom (Barron's 2025-07-01); JPMorgan expects less impact on Abbott than on Dexcom; Dexcom's IR speaks of 'the balance of economics between us and the durable-medical-equipment distributors'. Read as the distributors taking at least half, the set books half the excess, a 20.4% pass-through: 40% x 20.7% x 20.4% = 1.69% of CGM sales in FY2028 (the round-7 10% had no source), pending Kilian, charged with no cost relief in the Devices margin. The earlier 2.5% option is withdrawn: its claim that winning bidders press manufacturers on price has no source.

options.label: 1.69% of CGM sales (40% x 20.7% x 20.4% pass-through; booked placeholder)
options.reasoning: Half the OIG supplier excess reaches Abbott's price: a bid cut can take at most the 40.8% excess out of the channel, and Raymond James expects distributors to 'shoulder a good portion' with Abbott, the lower-cost player, better positioned.

options.label: No step (0%)
options.reasoning: Bids land near today's supplier acquisition costs, so Abbott's own selling price to suppliers does not move; the overpayment OIG found sits in the supplier channel, not with the manufacturer.

options.label: 0.83% of CGM sales (10% pass-through, the round-7 placeholder)
options.reasoning: Suppliers absorb almost all of the bid cut out of their margin above acquisition cost; the 10% has no source.

options.label: 3.38% of CGM sales (the whole 40.8% OIG excess passed to Abbott)
options.reasoning: Suppliers pass the whole bid cut back to the maker and keep their margin; an upper bound against Raymond James's reading that distributors take a good portion.

judgment_calls_for_kilian.recommendation: Kilian's decision (booked as before): 1.69% of CGM sales, half the OIG supplier excess
judgment_calls_for_kilian.why: The Medicare share is sized from public figures (years unmatched) and the pass-through is bounded by the OIG excess and read from analysts' statements on who bears the cut, with no number for Abbott; the options span -0.7% to +0.7% on the research target (12m).

judgment_calls_for_kilian.question: Which FY2027 growth for Libre CGM: the market pair less the international price cut, or a variant?
judgment_calls_for_kilian.context: FY2027 Diabetes Care ($8.6B FY2026; 60% international) is built from the forward market forecasts by region on Q3 2026 weights, now on one publisher's global / US pair (gate fix round 7): Fortune Business Insights' global CGM market 10.1% a year 2026-34 (updated 2026-11-02), with the US 40.5% of 2026 and no separate US rate, so both regions start at 10.1%. Kilian picked the 2pt blood-test haircut on his decision card (2026-11-18 7:38 PM ET, cmsg_01HdhANNPxz1f5xqDwR22cfLAPFTtCWpGgA1D4rR579bDi), and the set now books +11.07% a year: screening (79%: Cologuard and Exact's own blood test) at the colorectal cancer screening market 13.2% a year 2026-2036 (Meticulous Research, November 2026) less 2pt for blood tests taking share = 11.2%, and precision oncology (21%) at the cancer tumor profiling market 10.6% a year 2026-31 (MarketsandMarkets): 0.79 x 11.2% + 0.21 x 10.6% = 11.07%; FY2026-29 2,980/4,176/4,638/5,152. The haircut's size has no source: Guardant's Shield is growing fast (Q3 2026 screening revenue $67.6M vs $24.1M, 83,000 tests vs 24,000, FY2026 guided $233-238M, about 9% of the 2026 market) with no 2027 outlook, while Exact sells both test types (the CEO: its blood test launched in September, so 'it really did not have much impact in Q3', and its ASP is higher than Cologuard's). The old booking (+12.65%, screening at the market with no haircut) is now a sized option.

options.label: Kilian's pick (booked): +11.07%, 2pt blood haircut
options.reasoning: Cologuard grows a little below its market as Shield takes part of the screening growth; the 2pt size has no source and is Kilian's decision on 2026-11-18 (7:38 PM ET).

options.label: Old booking: +12.65%, screening at the market 13.2%
options.reasoning: Exact sells stool and blood tests, so its screening line grows with a market whose forecast already includes blood-based growth; the CEO says Cologuard 'continues to accelerate'.

options.label: +9.49%: 4pt haircut
options.reasoning: Shield's tests more than tripled in a year (+246% in Q3 2026) and its screening revenue is guided at $233-238M for 2026, so blood takes a larger part of the market's growth.

options.label: +9% a year FY2027-29: blood tests take share faster
options.reasoning: Blood-based tests are the fastest-growing CRC screening test type; Cologuard growth drops well below the market from FY2027.

options.label: +15% a year FY2027-29: Cologuard mid-teens holds
options.reasoning: The CEO says Cologuard 'grew mid-teens and continues to accelerate'; the mid-teens rate holds through FY2029.

judgment_calls_for_kilian.recommendation: Kilian's decision (booked): +11.07% a year FY2028-29, the 2pt blood-test haircut

judgment_calls_history.question: Which level for Abbott's corporate functions and plan benefit costs in FY2027-29?
judgment_calls_history.context: Corporate / unallocated (adjusted EBIT less segment operating earnings) has three filed parts in the segment-note reconciliation: share-based compensation (built at 1.5% of sales, the anchored FY2025 ratio), other income (about nil in FY2024-25) and corporate functions and plan benefit costs. That last line has no forward driver the company discloses: it was -$308M in FY2023, -$422M in FY2024, -$157M in FY2025 (10-K R89) and -$195M in 9M 2026 (10-Q R63), with Q4 FY2025 a +$20M credit, so it swings with pension and plan-benefit true-ups. The set books -$260M a year (the 9M 2026 annual rate) only as a placeholder; no real-world case picks between the filed levels, so this is Kilian's call. Q4 FY2026 corporate is separately set from the Q4 EPS guide midpoint (declared guide use).

options.label: -$260M a year (9M 2026 annual rate, booked placeholder)
options.reasoning: The latest filed level, including Exact's corporate overhead after the March 2026 close: 9M 2026 corporate functions and plan benefit costs -$195M (Q1 -65, Q2 -45, Q3 -85), at an annual rate -$260M.

options.label: -$157M a year (FY2025 level)
options.reasoning: FY2025, the last full filed year, showed -$157M including a +$20M Q4 plan-benefit credit; if those credits recur the line stays near FY2025. Engine-sized against the booked set.

options.label: -$422M a year (FY2024 level)
options.reasoning: FY2024 showed -$422M; a return of plan-benefit costs (pension expense) and the stand-alone costs around the end-2027 Nutrition separation could push the line back toward that level. Engine-sized against the booked set.

judgment_calls_history.recommendation: none: Kilian to choose (no real-world case separates the filed levels; -$260M is booked only as a placeholder)
judgment_calls_history.why: The line has no disclosed forward driver and has ranged from -$422M to -$157M in three filed years; the options span -1.3% to +0.8% on the research target (12m).
judgment_calls_history.status: withdrawn 2026-11-18 (gate fix round 2): corporate functions now sourced (FY2026 level grown with the FOMC PCE projection; 10-Q R60 pension), no placeholder card
